name: Citizenship by Descent (Jus Sanguinis)

requirements.blocker_text: Code de la Nationalite Nigerienne (Ordonnance 84-33, as amended by Ordonnance 99-17), Article 11: a legitimate child born to a Nigerien father OR a Nigerien mother acquires Nigerien nationality, as does a natural (non-marital) child whose established parent -- father or mother -- is Nigerien. This gender-neutral rule dates to the 1999 amendment, which equalized paternal and maternal lineage after the original 1984 code favored the father. Article 8 separately grants citizenship to anyone born in Niger with a direct first-degree ancestor also born there, and to foundlings of unknown parentage found in Niger.
requirements.fix_path: Establish the parental link to a Nigerien-citizen parent (or, for the birth-in-Niger route, to an ancestor born in Niger) through a birth certificate and the parent's citizenship documentation.

sources.title: Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative (NGO-hosted primary legal text) -- Code de la Nationalite Nigerienne, Article 11 (gender-neutral descent, 1999 amendment) and Article 8 (birth-in-Niger ancestry rule)
Wikipedia -- corroborates gender-neutral descent and confirms Niger allows dual nationality since the 2014 reform (Loi 2014-60)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Niger). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to an NGO-hosted copy of the primary legal text, tier 3, corroborated by Wikipedia, tier 4; Niger's own Journal Officiel publication of the code was not independently fetched -- disclosed gap. GENUINE, CONFIRMED FINDING (rare in this dataset): dual_citizenship_allowed is set to TRUE, not left null, because two independent sources agree Niger's 2014 reform (Loi 2014-60) explicitly introduced the right for Nigeriens to hold dual nationality -- a firmer confirmation than most other countries built in this dataset have received on this specific field. REGIONAL COMPARISON: Niger's gender-neutral descent rule (1999) came 4 years after Mali's equivalent 1995 reform (ml_citizenship_by_descent.json) -- both Sahelian neighbors modernized within the same rough window, a pattern worth noting rather than coincidence.
